title: Martin Grove, Longtime Columnist for The Hollywood Reporter, Dies at 83
full_text: Skip to main content By Mike Barnes Plus Icon Mike Barnes Senior Editor mikebarnes4 Follow Sign Up View All October 1, 2026 9:12am Martin Grove Courtesy of Grove Family Martin Grove, who wrote more than 3,300 columns for The Hollywood Reporter over 25 years as one of his era’s most respected and influential film experts, has died. He was 83. Grove died Tuesday at Providence Cedars-Sinai Tarzana Medical Center of cancer-related natural causes, his daughter, Universal Pictures vp media Alyson Grove, told THR . He inspired her to work in the business, she said. Grove’s “Hollywood Report” column, which centered on box office analysis, marketing and distribution, appeared on the pages of THR from July 1985 through January 2000. His “Filmmaker Focus” column, which showcased the art of making movies, then served as an exclusive THR.com feature through December 2010. Related Stories TV Peppino Mazzullo, Voice of Topo Gigio, the Italian Puppet on 'The Ed Sullivan Show,' Dies at 100 Movies John Grover, Film Editor on Six James Bond Movies, Dies at 87 “My dad truly loved his time at THR ,” his daughter said. The amiable Grove also appeared as a movie expert on CNN’s ShowBiz Today from 1989-2001 and as a movie analyst for CNNfn’s The Biz from 1996-2004, and his entertainment business reports could be heard weekday afternoons on the all-news Los Angeles radio station KNX from 1999-2004. In 2001, Grove taped luncheon interviews at Wolfgang Puck’s Spago in Beverly Hills with the likes of Ron Howard, Ridley Scott, Steven Soderbergh, Wolfgang Petersen and Michael Bay for the AMC series Behind the Screen . And from 1990-2008, he produced, wrote and provided the voiceovers for 90-second sponsored movie previews distributed to airlines including American, United, Delta, Northwest and TWA. Born on March 30, 1943, in Perth Amboy, New Jersey, Martin Allan Grove received his bachelor’s degree from Rutgers University, where he majored in art history and journalism and worked for the campus radio station, WRSU. En route to earning his master’s degree in screenwriting from NYU’s School of the Arts by taking night classes, he spent his days at ABC, where he handled radio network publicity and then business publicity for ABC television. As management, he helped keep WABC, New York’s top-rated radio station, on the air during several extended talent and engineering walkouts in 1967 by filling in on the graveyard shift for such popular DJs as Bruce Morrow (Cousin Brucie) and Dan Ingram. “As the strikes went on,” he said, “WABC created new jingles promoting ‘The Strikebound Sound of 77 WABC,’ and I had my own ‘Marty Grove’ jingle to use on the shows I did.” Grove later directed publicity for the advertising firm Foote, Cone & Belding, headed corporate communications and investor relations for 20th Century Fox in New York and Los Angeles and led marketing for Warner Bros. Television in Burbank (at Fox, he did marketing for its Movietone News library of newsreels as well). Before studios routinely announced box office figures, Grove served from 1985-95 as an Entertainment Tonight consultant for a Monday feature that projected grosses, and he appeared frequently on ET as a film expert during this period. Grove interviewed celebrities and filmmakers for THR ’s televised coverage of the 1987 Cannes Film Festival and anchored the paper’s TV coverage of the NATO/ShoWest theater owners conventions in Las Vegas from 1987-91. Starting in 1988, he hosted half-hour talk show episodes about Hollywood and two-minute commentaries about movies for Movietime, the cable network that later became E! Entertainment; produced, wrote and hosted the series For Your Consideration about Oscar and Golden Globes contenders on Time Warner Cable in New York and L.A.; and was a film industry analyst for the Financial News Network. During his career, Grove showed up on the NBC Nightly News , the CBS Evening News , ABC World News Tonight , Today , 20/20 , CNBC’s Power Lunch and Fox News programs was quoted in The New York Times , Wall Street Journal , Time , Washington Post , Sunday Times of London , Rolling Stone and Agence-France Presse . Since 2008, he served as CEO and president of ZAMM.com, for which he wrote, produced and voiced hundreds of movie preview videos as part of a content partnership with Amazon. A member of the WGA West, Grove sold screenplay pitches to Paramount and Columbia that he wrote and developed but that were not produced. He also authored a novel set in the world of network television, 10 pseudonymous mystery novels and a half-dozen pop-culture paperbacks, including an authorized biography of John Travolta, an instant biography of Elvis Presley published within days of his 1977 death and profiles of The Beatles, The Osmonds, Henry Winkler and Paul McCartney. Along the way, he still examined the estimated box office numbers every Sunday and the actuals every Monday. In addition to his daughter, survivors include his wife of 55 years, Marjorie; son Geoffrey; daughter-in-law Hilary; granddaughter Reesa; and grandson Rogan. THR

title: Kevin Feige Hails Theatrical Experience as ‘the Real Movie Magic’ at Will Rogers Motion Picture Pioneers Tribute
full_text: Breaking News MERGER APPROVED: Paramount Tentatively Sets Tuesday to Close Warner Bros. Deal Oct 1, 2026 9:09am PT Kevin Feige Hails Theatrical Experience as ‘the Real Movie Magic’ at Will Rogers Motion Picture Pioneers Tribute By Cynthia Littleton Plus Icon Cynthia Littleton Business Editor @Variety_Cynthia Latest Don’t Lie, Don’t Cry and Use Common Sense: Adam Levy, Judge Judy’s Son, Joins the Family Business With ‘Adam’s Law’ 1 week ago How NBCUniversal Television Thrives on Collaborative Energy Between Studios and Platforms: ‘We Cheer Each Other On’ 1 week ago Her Road to the Top: How NBCUniversal TV Studio Chief Pearlena Igbokwe Learned to Balance Business and Creative Instincts 1 week ago See All Ryan Miller / @captureimaging.com He’s a “great guy who’s incredibly humble” who has also produced 38 movies in 17 years that have delivered more than $35 billion at the box office. Twelve of those titles delivered more than $1 billion; three of them generated $2 billion apiece. Not to mention, Kevin Feige is the architect of the most meticulously crafted, interconnected cinematic universe in the history of motion pictures. Disney Entertainment chairman Alan Bergman reeled off those stunning stats (and admirable qualities) as he took part in Wednesday night’s tribute to Feige, president of Marvel Studios and chief creative officer of Marvel, who was honored with this year’s Pioneer of the Year laurel from the Will Rogers Motion Picture Pioneers Foundation . Related Stories Melissa McCarthy on Getting Serious for 'JonBenét Ramsey,' the Psychiatrist on Set and Hollywood's 'Bulls---’ Excuse for Why Comedies Don't Work Anymore Her Road to the Top: How NBCUniversal TV Studio Chief Pearlena Igbokwe Learned to Balance Business and Creative Instincts “Guardians of the Galaxy” star Chris Pratt and writer-director Jon Favreau were on hand at the Beverly Hilton hotel to laud the Marvel leader. Composer Michael Giacchino was there via video because of illness. Others who paid tribute in prerecorded reels include Marvel’s Louis D’Esposito and MCU stars Robert Downey Jr., Chris Evans, Hayley Atwell, Chris Hemsworth, Paul Bettany, Hailee Steinfeld, Pedro Pascal and Vanessa Kirby. Popular on Variety Feige was the star of the night but the conversation in the packed ballroom was dominated by the big news of the day, Paramount Skydance’s surprise news that Mattel CEO Ynon Kreiz is leaving the toymaker to join the Melrose plant as co-CEO with David Ellison. “He believes in the movies, and even more than that he believes in the people who make the movies,” Pratt told the crowd at the Beverly Hilton. The event raised $1.9 million for the Will Rogers Pioneers Assistance Fund, which helps those in the film exhibition community who need assistance. Also in the crowd were Disney chief Josh D’Amaro, AMC Theatres leader Adam Aron and Eduardo Acuna of Regal Cinemas, producer Scott Stuber among others. Favreau echoed Pratt’s comments about Feige’s passion for all things related to cinema. “The man loves movies. He listens to movie soundtracks in his car,” the “Iron Man” director told the crowd. “He’s driving down PCH blasting the ‘Ferngully’ soundtrack.” Feige took a bit of gentle ribbing about his love of custom baseball caps and other characteristics that have become his signature. From video, Giacchino introduced a large tiki band that emerged on stage to perform Marvel movie tunes with a Polynesian flair. The executive and producer lived up to his advance billing for humility in his remarks at the end of the night. And he had some thoughtful observations about what it is that makes moviegoing so special. He even name-checked his childhood haunt, the Rialto Theater in Westfield, New Jersey. (“Sitting in the dark, eating Twizzlers. I was hooked,” he recalled.) “Underneath all the technology and the spectacle, the years of work from development to post. It’s still the same thing: a group of people making something with others, and then a group of people sitting in the dark and experiencing it with others. That is the full process of a movie,” Feige said. “The final crucial part of that collaboration is the audience. Movies are an invitation to experience a story together. When a film connects and the crowd is cheering, laughing and crying together, that shared emotion is the final step in the process. That’s the real movie magic, You might even say it’s not a real movie without it,” he said. title: Jackie Chan, Anil Kapoor Films Among 335 National Winners at Asian Academy Creative Awards
full_text: Breaking News MERGER APPROVED: Paramount Tentatively Sets Tuesday to Close Warner Bros. Deal Oct 1, 2026 9:03am PT Jackie Chan, Anil Kapoor Films Among 335 National Winners at Asian Academy Creative Awards By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Sabu’s ‘Arrested Memory’ Leads Golden Horse Awards Nominations, Shu Qi’s ‘Girl’ Close Behind 3 hours ago Ballet Star Tiler Peck to Make London West End Debut in Susan Stroman’s ‘Little Dancer’ (EXCLUSIVE) 8 hours ago Venice Golden Lion Winner Milcho Manchevski’s ‘Sister Brother Manhole Cover’ Heads to Tokyo for World Premiere, Trailer Unveiled (EXCLUSIVE) 9 hours ago See All Golden Network Asia Films fronted by Jackie Chan and Anil Kapoor are among the 335 national winners named by the Asian Academy Creative Awards . “The Shadow’s Edge” won Best Feature Film for Chinese Mainland, and “Subedaar” won it for India. The winners come from 18 nations and territories and span 39 categories. They now move on to the international round. Grand winners will be named at the gala awards final at Singapore’s Capitol Theatre in December. Prime Video India and Astro Malaysia collected 19 each, and CNN took 15. Popular on Variety Chinese drama series “The Lead” won more categories than any other title, with six. They included Best Actress in a Leading Role for Liu Haocun. Best Drama Series, however, went to the bigger-budget “Legend of the Magnate.” Malaysia’s haul came with a note of loss. Horror feature “Malam Terlarang” (Forbidden Night) won four categories, among them Best Feature Film and Best Actress in a Supporting Role for Sofia Jane. Its Best Direction (Feature Film) win went to Norhanisham bin Muhammad, who died in May. Astro’s family crime drama “Good Boys Go to Heaven” added five Malaysian wins, taking both Best Actor and the drama series prize. In Japan, “Song of the Samurai” also won five categories but lost Best Drama Series to “Alice in Borderland.” Non took Best Actress for “Miss King.” China’s “Swords Into Plowshares” also collected four wins, as did Season 3 of India’s “The Family Man.” Bai Yu was named Best Actor in a Leading Role for Chinese Mainland. Taiwan broadcaster PTS also scored four wins with “Dogman.” The series took Best Drama Series as well as acting honors for Chang Hsiao Chuan and Tarcy Su. GMMTV’s “Enigma Black Stage” picked up four Thai wins. Scripted categories were hotly contested. Gemini Norawit Titicharoenrak was named Best Actor for “Ticket to Heaven,” while Mono’s Manatsanun Phanlerdwongsakul took Best Actress for “Sweet Dreams.” In the Philippines, Vice Ganda, one of the country’s biggest stars, had to get through an extra tie-breaker round before securing Best Actor for his performance in “Call Me Mother.” Nadine Lustre, who stars opposite him in that film, also advances, though her nod is for headlining Viu’s “Love, Siargao.” Animated feature “The Violinist” took Best Feature Film, Best Animation and Best Screenplay for Singapore. Its voice cast includes Tan Kheng Hua and Ayden Sng. Sng was separately named Best Actor in a Leading Role (Singapore) for the series “Double Helix.” Singaporean independent Refinery Media won three categories for lifestyle show “Man of the Hour.” CNN’s 15 wins came in the factual categories. One went to Kristie Lu Stout, a previous winner, for Best Factual Presenter (Thailand). She will go up against another past winner, Singapore’s Wei Du, who was recognized for CNA’s “Walk the Line: ICE Nation.” Awards chair Beverley McGarvey, president and streaming lead at Paramount ANZ, said the awards show every year how deep the region’s pool of talent and original ideas runs. “Our stories are becoming more confident, more distinctive and more influential, not only in their home markets but with audiences all around the world,” she said. McGarvey said that entry numbers were level with last year’s. She added that the size of the national winners field makes it the world’s biggest showcase of Asia-Pacific content. This year’s jurors came from 38 countries. The awards use a two-round system. A jury of senior industry figures from TV networks, streamers, production outfits, distributors, buyers and screen agencies first scores entries at the national level. It scores them again in the international round to choose the grand winners. title: David Ellison Wants CEO Mark Thompson To Remain At CNN After Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery Deal Closes
full_text: Skip to main content By Ted Johnson , Jill Goldsmith October 1, 2026 9:03am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Mark Thompson Photo by John Lamparski/Getty Images for Advertising Week New York Paramount CEO David Ellison wants Mark Thompson to remain at CNN after the Warner Bros. Discovery deal closes, a move that would settle at least some of the speculation over the future of the network under its incoming new owners. Talks between Ellison and Thompson are said to be in their early stages, according to sources familiar with the matter. The Wall Street Journal first reported on Ellison’s plans to retain Thompson, who was tapped to lead the network in 2023. Since then, he has sought to integrate the linear and digital operations while launching CNN’s All Access subscription and streaming service. Related Stories News CNN Again Removed As TV Pooler Set To Travel With Donald Trump News Warner Bros. Discovery Strikes Mega Content Deal With UK's ITV For TLC & Quest Shows Like 'Mock The Week', 'Dr. Pimple Popper', 'Salvage Hunters' Under Thompson, CNN also has continued to aggressively report on the Trump administration, while embarking on a lawsuit against the president after he banned the network and two other outlets from the White House grounds. The network also has defended its reporters in the face of attacks by the president, including its chief White House correspondent, Kaitlan Collins. Watch on Deadline The Journal also reported that Bari Weiss, the editor in chief of CBS News, was not expected to have a role in CNN. There has been speculation among current and former staffers at the network that Weiss could be given additional responsibilities after the deal close, as CBS News and CNN will now be sister networks. According to a financial filing earlier this year, CNN was expected to generate $1.8 billion in revenue for the 2026 fiscal year, and $600 million in profit. The network was estimated to reach $2.2 billion in revenue in 2030, with $700 million in profit. title: UTA Streamlines Film, TV and Talent Leadership; Matt Rice Rises to President of Filmed Entertainment Unit
full_text: Breaking News MERGER APPROVED: Paramount Tentatively Sets Tuesday to Close Warner Bros. Deal Oct 1, 2026 9:02am PT UTA Streamlines Film, TV and Talent Leadership; Matt Rice Rises to President of Filmed Entertainment Unit By Cynthia Littleton Plus Icon Cynthia Littleton Business Editor @Variety_Cynthia Latest Don’t Lie, Don’t Cry and Use Common Sense: Adam Levy, Judge Judy’s Son, Joins the Family Business With ‘Adam’s Law’ 1 week ago How NBCUniversal Television Thrives on Collaborative Energy Between Studios and Platforms: ‘We Cheer Each Other On’ 1 week ago Her Road to the Top: How NBCUniversal TV Studio Chief Pearlena Igbokwe Learned to Balance Business and Creative Instincts 1 week ago See All Courtesy of UTA UTA has taken a dramatic step to streamline the leadership of its film and TV lit and talent departments to reflect the industry trends of blurring lines between disciplines. As part of the change, agency veteran Matt Rice has been promoted to president of the new UTA Filmed Entertainment unit. In the new structure, UTA’s Allan Haldeman, Blair Kohan, Jay Gassner and Julien Thuan have been elevated to managing partners of Filmed Entertainment. UTA has named new department heads to lead key segments: Amanda Hymson and Jordan Lonner will lead Motion Picture Literary; Lucinda Moorhead and Mickey Berman will run TV Literary while talent will be steered by Hanley Baxter and John Sacks alongside longstanding talent chief Mike Jelline. Related Stories 'It's Time for My Voice': Jennifer Hudson on Reviving 'Dreamgirls,' Booking Tom Cruise for Her Talk Show and Writing Original Music Again Melissa McCarthy on Getting Serious for 'JonBenét Ramsey,' the Psychiatrist on Set and Hollywood's 'Bulls---’ Excuse for Why Comedies Don't Work Anymore Another new wrinkle is the formation of a Filmed Entertainment board that includes agency stalwarts including Jelline, Berman, Moorhead, Jason Burns, Marissa Devins, Dan Erlij, Chris Hart, Jason Heyman, Keya Khayatian, Rich Klubeck, Billy Lazarus, Gregory McKnight, David Park, Theresa Peters, Shani Rosenzweig and Larry Salz. Popular on Variety UTA chief executive David Kramer outlined the reasoning for the changes in a memo sent to agency staffers on Thursday morning “UTA has never been a place that waits for change — we anticipate where the industry is going and build for what comes next,” Kramer said. “As the business evolves and film and television increasingly converge, this team positions us to lead that evolution, unlock new possibilities for our clients and bring the full power of UTA to everyone we represent.” Rice joined UTA in 2002 after getting his start at the Broder Kurland literary agency. He’s one of the town’s top representatives of writers, directors and showrunners, including such notables as Phil Lord & Chris Miller, Michael Schur, Alec Berg, Bill Hader, Seth Rogen & Evan Goldberg, Will Forte, Justin Halpern & Patrick Schumacker, R. Scott Gemmill, James Gunn, Dan Goor, Chris McKenna & Erik Sommers, Adam Reed, Sebastian Maniscalco and Matt Rife. “This move reflects what sets UTA apart — a bold, collaborative and forward-thinking approach. I’m excited to build upon the work of this exceptional group of leaders and continue to deliver best-in-class representation to our clients,” Rice said. UTA’s shakeup of its longstanding departmental lines reflects the shifting sands for the content business as well as the business of representing boldface name talent. The growth in audience and influence among the largest social media platforms has revved up the creator economy and birthed a new breed of digital media superstar. All of this has challenged the traditional operations of Hollywood’s largest talent and management firms. Here is Kramer’s full memo: UTA has never been a place that waits for change — we anticipate where the industry is going and build for what comes next. With that in mind, we are announcing a streamlined, future-focused leadership structure for our Filmed Entertainment group which reflects the evolving business of film and television and will enable us to maximize opportunities for clients. By bringing together partners across Motion Picture Literary, Television Literary and Talent, we will continue to deliver unrivaled seamless client representation, sharpen the agency’s competitive edge and increase efficiency and collaboration. I’m thrilled to announce that Matt Rice has been elevated to President of Filmed Entertainment. Matt is a phenomenal agent and partner who has helped spearhead a transformative expansion of UTA’s television division. In his expanded role, he will lead overall strategy and execution across all areas of Filmed Entertainment. To support Matt and drive leadership across the entirety of the Filmed Entertainment group, we have elevated Allan Haldeman, Blair Kohan, Jay Gassner and Julien Thuan to the role of Managing Partner of Filmed Entertainment. This newly established leadership group will be critical to driving growth, connecting opportunities across our business and delivering exceptional results for clients as film and TV increasingly converge. To further capture market momentum and maximize client opportunities we have also established a Filmed Entertainment board. These senior partnerswill leverage their collective expertise, experience and deep industry relationships to aggressively pursue client development and new initiatives. Board members will include Mickey Berman, Jason Burns, Marissa Devins, Dan Erlij, Chris Hart, Jason Heyman, Mike Jelline, Keya Khayatian, Rich Klubeck, Billy Lazarus, Gregory McKnight, Lucinda Moorhead, David Park, Theresa Peters, Shani Rosenzweig, and Larry Salz. All of our Filmed Entertainment Department Heads play an integral part in ensuring our teams operate at the highest level in service of our clients. As we move to this new chapter, we are excited to appoint several new Department Heads across Filmed Entertainment: Amanda Hymson andJordan Lonner (Motion Picture Literary); Lucinda Moorhead and Mickey Berman (TV Literary); Hanley Baxter and John Sacks (Talent, alongside incumbent department head Mike Jelline). These agents have distinguished themselves through exceptional client representation and will be responsible for furthering the growth of their respective businesses. We’ve had an extraordinary year, with UTA clients behind some of 2026’s biggest box office hits and most acclaimed television productions, earning top honors at the Academy Awards, Emmys, Golden Globes and Tonys. We are building from a position of immense strength, and this new leadership structure is designed to carry that momentum forward and position us for even greater success. Please join me in congratulating our new leadership for Filmed Entertainment. We have so much to be proud of and I can’t wait to see this team take us to new heights in the coming year. title: WIF Honors Set to Celebrate Salma Hayek Pinault, Pamela Abdy and ‘Josephine’
full_text: × Skip to main content By Kirsten Chuba Plus Icon Kirsten Chuba Events Editor kirstenchuba Follow Sign Up View All October 1, 2026 9:00am Salma Hayek Pinault, Pam Abdy and Gemma Chan Jeff Spicer/Getty Images; Michael Buckner/Variety/Getty Images; Earl Gibson III/Dick Clark Productions/Getty Images The honorees for Women in Film ‘s annual WIF Honors have been set, with Pamela Abdy, Adria Arjona, Beth de Araújo, Gemma Chan and Salma Hayek Pinault all being celebrated. The event, taking place at the Beverly Hilton on Nov. 5, recognizes those who are driving gender equity across the industry, while also serving as WIF’s largest fundraiser of the year. Abdy, co-chair and CEO of Warner Bros. Motion Picture Group, will receive the inaugural Vanguard Award, a recognition for a leader whose career embodies the qualities that move the industry forward. The honor will be presented by Nancy Meyers , who is currently working on a new movie for Warner Bros. title: ‘Rolling Loud: The Movie’ Review: Owen Wilson Plays a Very Bad Dad in a Tone-Deaf Would-Be Comedy
full_text: × Skip to main content By Frank Scheck Plus Icon Frank Scheck View All October 1, 2026 9:00am 'Rolling Loud: The Movie' Ketchup Entertainment An underage teenager gets snuck into a hip-hop music festival headlined by Travis Scott and soon goes missing, his desperate father frantically attempting to find him before it’s too late. No, it’s not a harrowing drama based on the tragic 2021 real-life events at Scott’s Astroworld concert in Texas, where 10 concertgoers were killed in a fatal crowd crush. Instead, Rolling Loud: The Movie is…a comedy. Discuss among yourselves. Rolling Loud: The Movie The Bottom Line A bad idea, terribly executed. Release date : Friday, October 2 Cast : Owen Wilson, Matt Rife, Christine Ko, Christian Convery, Jolene, Henry Winkler, Travis Scott Director-screenwriter : Jeremy Garelick Rated R, 1 hour 35 minutes To say that this effort written and directed by Jeremy Garelick ( The Wedding Ringer , Murder Mystery 2 ) — who is modestly described in the film’s press notes as “reinventing Hollywood comedy with brain, heart, and guts” — comes across as tone-deaf is an understatement. Even if you ignore the disturbing parallels to past events, this story of a dad attempting to bond with his 13-year-old son by irresponsibly sneaking him into the popular hip-hop music festival of the title while lying to his wife and the festival’s security personnel just feels icky. Did I mention it’s a true story? Related Stories Movies 'Practical Magic 2' Summons $30M to End Spider-Man's Streak at No. 1 Movies 'Practical Magic 2' Whips Up $4.7M in Box Office Previews Yes, the filmmaker apparently did take his 13-year-old to the festival, filled with people walking around in various states of undress and many of them using drugs, against his wife’s wishes. And he did lose contact with his son, unable to reach him because of the lack of cell phone reception. Apparently, rather than feeling chastened, he thought: “What a great idea for a movie!” Of course, it still could have worked if the film actually proved funny. Instead, it’s a witless, moronic, slapstick-filled mediocrity that basically serves as a feature-length commercial for the popular music festival where parts of it were filmed (Live Nation is among the production companies). To that end, the film features not only Scott, playing a recliner-chair-loving version of himself (don’t ask), but also such real-life hip-hop stars as Sexyy Red, Ski Mask the Slump God, and Ty Dolla $ign, none of whom are likely to enlarge their fan base. Wilson plays hapless furniture salesman Hank — he works at “Raymond & Ferguson” — who tells his wife Melanie (Jolene) that he’s taking their son Zion (Christian Convery) to their lake house, but instead brings him to Rolling Loud. There he runs into his co-worker Terry (comedian Matt Rife , managing to make his character as annoying as his stand-up), whom he had just been ordered to fire by their boss ( Henry Winkler , squandering some of that good will from Barry ). Distracted by Terry, Hank doesn’t think much of it when Zion excuses himself to go to the bathroom. But he becomes increasingly anxious when his son fails to reappear, and that’s when the would-be comic complications ensue. They include an episode in which Hank retreats to a quiet room, only to discover that his lying conversation to his wife has been broadcast to a disapproving crowd outside; a physical altercation with security guards when he attempts to report his son missing; and accidentally throwing Linda (Christine Ko), a festival volunteer worker, off of a Ferris wheel, injuring a wheelchair-bound bystander in the process. And, of course, Hank also accidentally takes drugs and begins tripping. And the volunteer strips naked to distract the security guards, revealing a forest-level growth of pubic hair in the process. (The appealing Ko, who provides some genuine amusement in her role, deserved better). It’s all about as laborious as it sounds, with Wilson, utilizing his familiar style of motor-mouthed pathos and desperation, working very hard to infuse comic energy into the strained proceedings. By the time he gets onstage with Scott and then disastrously leaps into the mosh pit, all you’re thinking is that he needs to collaborate with Wes Anderson again, and as soon as possible. As for Scott, if he survived the fallout from Astroworld, he can survive this. Adams, Dan Kaplow, Michael Rapino, Matt Rife, Pasquale Rotella, Christina Shams, Matt Philip Whelan, Matt Zingler Director of photography: Bradford Lipson Production designer: Kathrin Eder Composer: Chanda Dancy Costume designer: Wlaa Elashkar Casting: Findley Davidson, Mary Vernieu Rated R, 1 hour 35 minutes THR

The festival has also set Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi’s “La Bola Negra” as its Friday Spotlight and Tony Gilroy’s “ Behemoth !” as its Sunday Spotlight. As previously announced , the festival will open with Jesse Eisenberg’s “The Debut.” Martin McDonagh, Brad Bird, Seth Rogen , Rosalind Eleazar, Guitarricadelafuente and casting directors Adam Caldwell and Bernard Telsey will be honored at this year’s festival. Billie Jean King and Bill Pullman are among the special guests. Caldwell and Telsey will receive the festival’s Special Achievement in Casting Award and join a post-screening Q&A. Gilroy will be on hand for a post-screening conversation following Searchlight Pictures’ “Behemoth!” where Pedro Pascal plays a gifted cellist and former child prodigy who returns to Los Angeles after two decades on the road to record film scores and confront his complicated family history. McDonagh will receive the Director Spotlight Award for “Wild Horse Nine,” also from Searchlight. Set just before the 1973 Chilean coup, the film stars John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell as longtime CIA agents sent from Santiago to Easter Island, where they confront their dark pasts and a conspiracy unfolding around them. Bird will receive the Spotlight Animation Award for Netflix’s “Ray Gunn,” a passion project more than 30 years in the making. Bird wrote and directed the sci-fi noir, which is set in Metropia, a city where humans and aliens live side by side. Rogen will receive the MFF Artistic Achievement Award at an “In Conversation with Seth Rogen” event covering several of his films at the festival. He stars in Olivia Wilde’s A24 film “The Invite” alongside Wilde, Penélope Cruz and Edward Norton, playing one of two married couples whose relationships are tested by a dinner party that grows more unpredictable as the night goes on. Rogen also produced Leah Nelson’s animated film “Tangles” with Lauren Miller Rogen, Evan Goldberg and others. Based on Sarah Leavitt’s graphic memoir, it follows a young artist who moves home to care for her mother after an Alzheimer’s diagnosis. Rogen will join Nelson and Miller Rogen for a post-screening conversation. Eleazar will receive the Breakthrough Actor Award for A24’s “Misty Green,” written and directed by Chris Rock. In her first leading film role, she plays Misty, a once-successful actress whose career has stalled. She is fighting to win back her place in Hollywood while dealing with financial trouble, broken relationships and her own self-destructive streak. The annual Songwriters and Composers Panel will feature Ari Balouzian (“Primetime,” “You Can See Everything”), Lesley Barber (“Gail”), Jesse Eisenberg (“The Debut”), Lukas Frank (“Behemoth!”), Guitarricadelafuente (“La Bola Negra”), Daniel Pemberton (“Ink,” “Project Hail Mary”), Christopher Spelman (“Paper Tiger”) and Diane Warren (“Maserati: The Brothers”). “Toy Story 5” production designer Bob Pauley will lead a masterclass on his more than three decades at Pixar. Pauley was part of the original “Toy Story” creative team, designed Buzz Lightyear for the 1995 film and has worked on all five installments. He will also lead a drawing demonstration focused on new characters from “Toy Story 5.” Tennis legend Billie Jean King will attend with Liz Garbus and Elizabeth Wolff’s documentary “Give Me the Ball!” The film uses rare archival footage and candid interviews to examine the victories, struggles and personal sacrifices behind her tennis career and her fight for equality in sports and beyond. King will sit down with festival founder and board chair Sheila Johnson for a one-on-one post-screening conversation on Sunday, Oct. 18. Finally, Pullman will attend with “Everybody Digs Bill Evans,” Grant Gee’s unconventional portrait of the jazz pianist. Set in 1961, the film follows Evans (Anders Danielsen Lie) after the sudden death of his bassist and close collaborator Scott LaFaro, when grief drives him to stop playing and retreat from New York to his family home. MFF advisory board members Albert Berger and Ron Yerxa executive produce. The full Middleburg Film Festival lineup and honorees are below. title: UTA Sets New Leadership Structure For Filmed Entertainment Division Under President Matt Rice
full_text: Skip to main content By Matt Grobar Matt Grobar Senior Film Reporter More Stories By Matt Joachim Rønning Sets Horror Film ‘System’ With Spooky Pictures & Image Nation Studios Neon Counters A24’s SCP Foundation Movie With “Open-Source” Project To Release Under Creative Commons License 20th Century Studios Acquires Horror Package ‘Every House Is Haunted’ From Netflix; ‘Don’t Move’s Adam Schindler & Brian Netto Directing View All October 1, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Matt Rice, newly appointed President of UTA's Filmed Entertainment division Sonali Ohrie UTA on Thursday announced a comprehensive reorganization of its Filmed Entertainment Division, elevating Matt Rice to serve as its President. A longtime partner at the agency who most recently served as head of its TV department, Rice is known for his work with top writer, producer, director, talent and comedy clients like Phil Lord & Chris Miller, Mike Schur, Alec Berg, Bill Hader, Seth Rogen & Evan Goldberg, among others. “Matt is a phenomenal agent and partner who has helped spearhead a transformative expansion of UTA’s television division. In his expanded role, he will lead overall strategy and execution across all areas of Filmed Entertainment,” said CEO David Kramer in an internal memo to staff this morning. Related Stories Agencies UTA Signs 'Brian' Filmmaker Will Ropp Agencies UTA Signs 'Club Kid' Star Reggie Absolom In addition to Rice’s role, UTA has announced the promotion of Allan Haldeman, Blair Kohan, Jay Gassner and Julien Thuan to Managing Partners of Filmed Entertainment. Amanda Hymson and Jordan Lonner are now heads of Motion Picture Literary, with Lucinda Moorhead and Mickey Berman heading up TV Lit, and Hanley Baxter and John Sacks joining the incumbent Mike Jelline to head up the Talent department. Watch on Deadline Additionally, UTA today announced the formation of a Filmed Entertainment board, consisting of senior partners who, per Kramer, “will leverage their collective expertise, experience and deep industry relationships to aggressively pursue client development and new initiatives.” Board members include Mickey Berman, Jason Burns, Marissa Devins, Dan Erlij, Chris Hart, Jason Heyman, Mike Jelline, Keya Khayatian, Rich Klubeck, Billy Lazarus, Gregory McKnight, Lucinda Moorhead, David Park, Theresa Peters, Shani Rosenzweig, and Larry Salz. Kramer emphasized, in his memo to staff, that the reorg is intended to “increase efficiency and collaboration,” thereby maximizing client opportunities and sharpening “the agency’s competitive edge” amidst a rapidly evolving entertainment landscape. Kramer said that “UTA has never been a place that waits for change,” calling the new leadership structure “streamlined” and “future-focused.” He went on to say, “We’ve had an extraordinary year, with UTA clients behind some of 2026’s biggest box office hits and most acclaimed television productions, earning top honors at the Academy Awards, Emmys, Golden Globes and Tonys. We are building from a position of immense strength, and this new leadership structure is designed to carry that momentum forward and position us for even greater success.” Kramer’s assessment echos comments he made about the agency’s “record-breaking year,” “strength” and “momentum” in an Aug. 26 memo, in which he hit back at a Variety article about recent UTA client departures, which alleged internal anxiety, accusing the author of unprofessional bias. ( Variety ‘s parent company, Penske Media Corporation, also owns Deadline .) Read the full memo below: UTA has never been a place that waits for change — we anticipate where the industry is going and build for what comes next. With that in mind, we are announcing a streamlined, future-focused leadership structure for our Filmed Entertainment group which reflects the evolving business of film and television and will enable us to maximize opportunities for clients. By bringing together partners across Motion Picture Literary, Television Literary and Talent, we will continue to deliver unrivaled seamless client representation, sharpen the agency’s competitive edge and increase efficiency and collaboration. I’m thrilled to announce that Matt Rice has been elevated to President of Filmed Entertainment . title: Grammy Asian Pop Category Will Go Forward, CEO Says: ‘We Understand This Conclusion Will Not Satisfy Everyone’
full_text: Breaking News MERGER APPROVED: Paramount Tentatively Sets Tuesday to Close Warner Bros. Deal Oct 1, 2026 8:59am PT Grammy Asian Pop Category Will Go Forward, CEO Says: ‘We Understand This Conclusion Will Not Satisfy Everyone’ By Jem Aswad Plus Icon Jem Aswad Executive Editor, Music jemaswad Latest Sia Sells 50% of Music Catalog to Pophouse in $180 Million Partnership Deal 2 hours ago Billy Joel Gives Health Update After Brain Surgery: ‘I’m OK — It Sounds a Lot Worse Than It Actually Is’ 1 day ago LCD Soundsystem Announces 2026 NYC Residency — Including 100th Residency Show 1 day ago See All HYBE Grammy chief Harvey Mason Jr. has issued a statement in which he says the Awards’ controversial newest category, Asian Pop, will go forward for the 2027 ceremony. Mason had previously signaled that the Recording Academy was reconsidering the new category in the wake of decidedly split reactions after it was announced in June. BTS in particular objected to the category , implying that it effectively ghetto-izes a genre of music more than highlighting it and saying they will not submit their music for Grammy consideration in 2027. Related Stories Her Road to the Top: How NBCUniversal TV Studio Chief Pearlena Igbokwe Learned to Balance Business and Creative Instincts 'It's Time for My Voice': Jennifer Hudson on Reviving 'Dreamgirls,' Booking Tom Cruise for Her Talk Show and Writing Original Music Again “We hope our music can be heard and loved for what it is, rather than being divided by region or language,” the group said in a statement. Popular on Variety However, Mason is unequivocal about the award going forward, at least for 2027, based on conversations with multiple people in the community. “Over the past several weeks the Academy has been conducting listening sessions and have been in dialogue with leaders of the Asian music community,” Mason’s statement reads in full. “The journey has been rewarding and inspiring. Our organization is at its best when we engage deeply with music people and go the extra mile to understand their lived experiences. “In this case, we heard candid feedback from people in our community who don’t support the continuation of this category. We also heard from people who didn’t have accurate information about the category, and having space to clear up misperceptions has been especially valuable. But by far, the loudest feedback we heard was from people who were enthusiastic supporters of the category, fellow music creators expressing their encouragement for keeping it. “We understand this conclusion will not satisfy everyone, and that never feels good. But at the same time, we are confident it’s the right conclusion for the music community overall. As is the case with all our categories, we will continue to diligently engage with the music community and keep striving to honor this music — and all music — in the best possible way. We look forward to celebrating the Asian Pop Music Performance nominees at the 2027 Grammy Awards.” The Academy also noted that it has received a “robust” number of submissions for the category, signaling strong interest in its first year. The introduction of the award revived a familiar issue with the Grammys ’ genre-specific awards. While the intent may be to recognize music in a certain genre or language, many people within that community feel that it actually ends up being exclusionary, with voters relegating music or artists into those genre categories rather than more-mainstream ones; this has been a common complaint with regard to the Latin Grammys. While BTS has been nominated for Grammy Awards five times, in pop and other categories, the group has never won. “Golden,” from the smash film “KPop Demon Hunters” and performed by the fictional group Huntr/x (vocalists EJAE, Audrey Nuna, and Rei Ami), is widely considered the first KPop Grammy win, taking the award for best song written for visual media earlier this year, although it did not win for best song. title: CNN Chief Mark Thompson May Stay On After Sale — Though Contract Talks Are Early
full_text: × Skip to main content By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All October 1, 2026 8:50am CNN chief Mark Thompson Dimitrios Kambouris/Getty Images CNN may have more stability than some had feared under the combined Paramount-Warner Bros. David Ellison has held discussions with CNN CEO Mark Thompson about keeping the veteran executive in charge of the cable news channel, a source familiar with the matter says. The contract talks, however, are said to be very early, and there is no assurance that they can come to terms on a new deal. No change in leadership is expected at deal close, with Thompson’s current contract to lead CNN running into next year. The Wall Street Journal , which first reported the news, said that Thompson wants assurances that he will have autonomy over the global news brand, including on editorial matters. CNN will have an “editorial independence board” once the deal closes , with a group of journalists establishing guiding principles for the news outlet, and resolving any disputes with corporate leadership. If Thompson and Ellison are able to come to terms on a new deal, it would come as a sigh of relief to many CNN talent, who have been fearful of a dramatic overhaul at the channel post-merger, especially given Bari Weiss’ aggressive changes at CBS News. That doesn’t mean CNN won’t undergo changes under the combined company, but it does mean that Thompson will be able to continue executing on the digital reboot that he is in the middle of overseeing. While CNN’s linear ratings have been challenged in recent years, it remains a profit center among the WBD cable channels, filings show. Those profits will be particularly important as the combined company seeks to pay down an estimated $80 billion debt load. That said, one observer says that the merger will almost certainly require some level of consolidation between CBS News and CNN, though the devil may be in the details as things move forward. THR

title: What Ratings Issues? NBCU Telemundo Chair Touts World Cup Success for Live TV
full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All October 1, 2026 8:30am Luis Fernández Courtesy of NBCUniversal Telemundo Enterprises Luis Fernández , chairman of Spanish-language media powerhouse NBCUniversal Telemundo Enterprises and former Telemundo news chief, was one of the high-profile keynote speakers on Thursday afternoon at the sixth edition of Iberseries & Platino Industria in the Spanish capital, Madrid . In his appearance, he spent some time modestly taking a victory lap for Telemundo’s success with the soccer World Cup 2026, as well as touting the power of live and linear TV. Telemundo is part of entertainment company NBCUniversal, which is owned by Comcast but is scheduled to be spun off by the cable and telecom giant next year. “The FIFA football World Cup was the most-watched sports feature in Spanish [in the U.S.]. We never had those ratings,” Fernández told the Madrid event during his appearance entitled “Leadership, relevance and transformation of the Spanish-language audiovisual industry.” He particularly lauded the combined World Cup offerings across both streaming and linear services, emphasizing: “We were able to bring together Telemundo and Peacock, our streaming platform. Five out of the 10 most-watched programs on Peacock were events that happened during the World Cup.” Fernández also told the Iberseries crowd that based on how the World Cup was presented and consumed, his company’s advertising sales team signaled to him that they were expecting better Los Angeles Summer Olympics 2028 ad momentum than previously thought. The exec on Thursday further touted the importance of constant reinvention in the media and entertainment sector. “This industry has to reinvent every year, every month, every day,” he said. “And if you’re not adapting and reinventing yourself, you will be out of the system.” That means rethinking approaches and taking some risks. “If we fight, if we work, are bold and fearless, and also creative, we’ll be able” to succeed, he concluded. Luis Fernández at Iberseries 2026 As one example of the change he has brought to Telemundo, Fernández pointed to his early efforts to move beyond the image as a reality TV-centric broadcaster despite some initial skepticism within the company. “I was thinking of what we could do to improve the channel, to be more competitive, and to be more relevant,” he said. “We have reality TV, but we also have news, we have sports, we have fiction. So we had to get rid of that image that had formed.” How does the Telemundo chair feel about the outlook for linear TV versus streaming? “I think that streaming services are our rivals and our competitors, and I think that linear TV really has a lot of power in live shows,” Fernández offered. “The streaming services eventually will be able to be good at live TV, but right now, live TV is something where we have much more to offer.” Pointing to the World Cup again, he also shared: “I always hate when people say that linear or traditional TV is falling in viewership, ratings.” It will not surprise you that, in this context, Fernández also told Iberseries about his interest in continuing to offer up sports programming, including beyond soccer. “For me, that’s one of the key pillars of our strategy for the upcoming years,” he emphasized. “Sports licensing is one of the things that we’re investing in.” Asked about his view on AI, the exec replied: “It is an opportunity.” Without going into too much detail, he mentioned that the media space has always faced technological changes. title: Pro ‘Fortnite’ Gamer Cody ‘Clix’ Conrod Launches New Holding Company Full Box to Align Owned Businesses, Collabs and Philanthropy (EXCLUSIVE)
full_text: Breaking News MERGER APPROVED: Paramount Tentatively Sets Tuesday to Close Warner Bros. Deal Oct 1, 2026 8:30am PT Pro ‘Fortnite’ Gamer Cody ‘Clix’ Conrod Launches New Holding Company Full Box to Align Owned Businesses, Collabs and Philanthropy (EXCLUSIVE) By Jennifer Maas Plus Icon Jennifer Maas TV Business Writer @jmaasaronson Latest Pro ‘Fortnite’ Gamer Cody ‘Clix’ Conrod Launches New Holding Company Full Box to Align Owned Businesses, Collabs and Philanthropy (EXCLUSIVE) 20 minutes ago Fugitive Films Co-Founder, Former MTV Scripted Boss Launch Romance-Focused Vertical Content Studio, Rommi (EXCLUSIVE) 2 hours ago Author Chloe Gong on ‘Eyes of Kings’ ending, ‘Deadlock’ debut and how she wants ‘These Violent Delights’ adapted for TV or film 5 days ago See All Full Box Professional “Fornite” player and star gamer Cody “ Clix ” Conrod has launched Full Box Inc., a creator-led holding company to encompasses his nine businesses, ventures and community initiatives A nod to the sport itself, the name “Full Box” comes directly from the massive Epic Games-developed online game, where the term describes surrounding an opponent with control, skill and competitive execution. Per Full Box, the name “reflects both the competitive mindset that has defined [Conrod’s] career and the company’s approach to building a complete business ecosystem around a creator.” Related Stories Melissa McCarthy on Getting Serious for 'JonBenét Ramsey,' the Psychiatrist on Set and Hollywood's 'Bulls---’ Excuse for Why Comedies Don't Work Anymore 'It's Time for My Voice': Jennifer Hudson on Reviving 'Dreamgirls,' Booking Tom Cruise for Her Talk Show and Writing Original Music Again Joining Conrod at Full Box is Darren Glover, who spent six years building the gaming division at VaynerSports and served as Conrod’s first agent. Glove is set as Full Box CEO while Conrod serves as founder and chief creative officer and continues to compete and stream at the highest level of “ Fortnite .” Popular on Variety Full Box is focusing its holdings around three pillars: Operating Companies, Full Box Ventures and Impact. Built around Conrod’s commitment to giving back to the community he grew up with, Full Box Inc.’s Impact arm houses the Dr3amin Access Fund, a career development initiative providing kids with gaming PCs, hardware and programming designed to create pathways into competitive gaming, content creation and game development. The Fund formalizes Conrod’s longstanding grassroots efforts, which delivered more than $250,000 in gaming equipment through Clixmas, his large-scale holiday event, in 2025. “When we’re talking about new talent in the space, little short story: A gaming computer that I gave away around two years ago to a kid that was on 60 FPS, playing on a console, had no earnings. I gave him a Clixmas computer, and now he’s literally here in Belgium competing for $10 million right next to me, and he made over $150,000,” Conrod told Variety during an interview out of the Fortnite Global Championship last month. “So that one kid, his name is Joshreyli , happened off of me giving away, I think at that time was like 40 computers. So as time gets on, and now that it’s an official thing where people could now give us money in the Dr3amin Access Fund, and we could give that back, how many more kids can we help elevate and give access to, where they could actually become that? So these next five years is really just continuing to build it.” To date, Full Box Inc.’s Operating Companies division is comprised of owned businesses including: ● Clix Gaming, a content and production company spanning live streaming, competitive gaming, brand partnerships, and interactive digital experiences across Fortnite and Roblox. ● Clix Creative: A creator-led game studio building experiences within the competitive Fortnite ecosystem, built around ranked play, personal progression and tournaments. ● Dr3amin Clothing, the apparel and lifestyle brand inspired by Conrod’s personal journey. Full Box Ventures currently supports: ● Reach Clipping: The fastest-growing clipping agency on Content Rewards, helping creators and brands scale short-form distribution through performance-based clipping campaigns. ● Real Sports App: A booming social sports platform combining live scores and play-by-play with community, conversation and gaming at its core. ● Rorra: A next-generation water filtration company focused on making cleaner water more accessible. ● TapCaps: A brand co-founded alongside fellow creator Lacy, blending gaming and mainstream culture through limited-edition blind-box collectibles that double as clickable fidget toys and functional keyboard keycaps. ● XSET: A gaming lifestyle brand and media network where Conrod serves as a competitive player and co-owner. Glover says the overall Full Box business is made up of multiple revenue streams which are all built around, but not beholden to, Conrod’s “Fortnite” presence. “‘Fortnite,’ Roblox, ‘Minecraft,’ and ‘Grand Theft Auto’ are the only games that you can earn within the game itself,” Glover says. “So our business model is vertically integrated, which is very unique in the gaming world, where there are lots of people that make content about video games and they monetize on the media of the content, which is great. That’s a super simple way, but that’s a really bumpy road to create a business around that. ‘Fortnite’ gives you the ability to make money by playing the game. You’re creating content about the game. We have a creator code; that’s people putting in an affiliate link in the store when they buy something. They’re supporting Clix by putting in code Clix, which is a whole different content model and a fun thing that Cody has created are these, ‘Use Code Clix’ commercials.” Glover adds: “So we have an affiliate link model from all the commerce that’s happening inside of the store. We have games and experiences that we’re building with Clix Creative that we monetize specifically based on engagement, very similar to a YouTube model… So we’re making revenue for the business by players playing our maps and experiences. So we we’ve got this like very cool model that we make content about the game and we make content within the game. So for us, it’s not about trying to predict where the game goes.” This includes not only an ongoing collaboration with “Fortnite” maker Epic Games, but also one of its major investors, Disney. “We have a really good relationship with Disney,” Glover says. “I just saw Josh [D’Amaro], the CEO, last Friday, and praised him for his belief in ‘Fortnite.’ So for us, it’s not about trying to predict where they go. title: ‘Trailer Park Boys’ Actor Michael Smith Has Sexual Assault Charge Dismissed
full_text: Skip to main content By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All October 1, 2026 8:03am Michael Smith as Bubbles (center) is flanked by fellow cast members John Paul Tremblay and Robb Wells. Netflix Logo text Mike Smith, the Nova Scotia actor best known for playing Bubbles on the Trailer Park Boys comedy , has had a sexual assault charge against him dismissed. A three-day sexual assault trial in Dartmouth, Nova Scotia began Thursday, but Judge Jill Hartlen called a halt to the case after crown prosecutors declined to present any evidence, according to the CBC News website on Thursday. “The court has dismissed the charge against Michael Smith, concluding the legal proceedings that began in October 2025 regarding an allegation dating to December 2017,” Trailer Park Boys Inc., a Nova Scotia-based company that produces the series and in which Smith is one of three directors, said in a statement obtained by The Hollywood Reporter. Related Stories TV Netflix's New Releases Coming in October 2026 TV 'East of Eden' Review: A Terrifying Florence Pugh Towers Over Zoe Kazan's Accomplished Netflix Adaptation of the John Steinbeck Classic The company also has as directors Trailer Park Boys co-stars John Paul Tremblay, who plays Julian, and Robert Wells, who plays Ricky. The company added: “Now that he (Smith) is cleared of this matter, Mike is resuming his responsibilities with Trailer Park Boys Incorporated.” Bubbles, Julian and Ricky and the rest of their Sunnyvale Trailer Park crew featured in the cult Canadian mockumentary about three petty criminals running scams from their Halifax business. The franchise included a TV series that streamed on Netflix and movies. Smith stepped away from Trailer Park Boys Inc. in Oct. 2025 when he was charged with one count of sexual assault stemming from an alleged incident in 2017, and pleaded not guilty. The CBC, Canada’s public broadcaster, on its online news site said an unnamed complainant against Smith in a statement said she was “unwilling to sacrifice my mental health” by testifying during the trail. The Trailer Park Boys was created in 2001 by Barry Dunn, Wells, Tremblay and Mike Clattenburg and originally launched on Canada’s Showcase channel. The series ended its Canadian TV run in 2008. Netflix picked up the Trailer Park Boys property in 2014. THR

title: Bennington College, Alma Mater of Brett Easton Ellis and Donna Tartt, Launches Screenwriting MFA
full_text: × Skip to main content By Mia Galuppo Plus Icon Mia Galuppo Senior Entertainment Reporter miagaluppo Follow Sign Up View All October 1, 2026 8:00am Bennington College Bennington College Bennington College has long been known for graduating literary talent, with notable alumni like Brett Easton Ellis, Donna Tartt and Kiran Desai. Now, the Vermont school is looking to break new screenwriting stars. Bennington is launching an MFA in screenwriting, planning for a two-year low-residency program that will see a small cohort of students participate in four ten-day residencies, two at Bennington in Vermont and two in Los Angeles, as well as eight ten-week online courses. “This is a unique screenwriting MFA, perfectly suited to our times,” said Theodore Braun, the director of the new Bennington program. “It blends the rigor of residential education with the flexibility of low residency, giving writers anywhere access to Bennington’s humanistic tradition of the liberal arts, elite screenwriter mentors, and the immersive professional energy of Los Angeles.” Related Stories Business Disney+ Strikes Streaming Bundle and Content-Sharing Deal With Indonesia's Vidio The Show Formerly Known as 'South Park' 'South America' Takes on the Literal Dicks of Big Tech Billionaires in New Episode Braun notes that the inaugural class will be “just six gifted, driven writers-students who are serious about building a body of work and launching a professional screenwriting career.” As for faculty, Bennington has lined up working writers that include The Holdovers writer David Hemingson and Bridgerton writer-producer Janet Lin, as well as Alexa Alemanni ( The Librarians ), Malia Scotch Marmo ( Hook ) and Aaron Rahsaan Thomas ( S.W.A.T. and Friday Night Lights ). Over the course of the program, students will produce feature scripts, spec television episodes, an original pilot and series bible, among other projects. The program will culminate in a capstone industry showcase in Los Angeles. Bennington has already graduated several well-known screenwriters, including Melissa Rosenberg, responsible for the Twilight adaptations, and Sofia Alvarez, who is behind the To All the Boys I’ve Loved Before films. “I think what Bennington excels at — its whole reason for being — is finding, nurturing, and empowering original voices,” offers Rosenberg. “That and the spirit of collaboration make it a wonderful place to launch this new MFA.” THR

title: Disney’s Worlds Collide Tour Hits All the Right Notes With ‘Descendants,’ ‘Zombies’ and ‘Camp Rock’ Stars
full_text: × Skip to main content By Kimberly Nordyke , Brianna Nordyke , Brooklyn Nordyke October 1, 2026 7:32am The Worlds Collide cast Courtesy Disney Concerts It’s safe to say there are a lot of tired — but really, really happy — kids in Los Angeles on Monday morning. Crypto.com Arena was filled on Monday night with adults and kids — from toddlers to teens — for a jam-packed, fast-paced, high-energy show courtesy of Disney . Eight cast members from three of the company’s hit movie franchises — Descendants , Zombies and Camp Rock — performed a three-hour show (with a 20-minute intermission) featuring all the big songs from those movies and then some, with the whole thing ending around 10 p.m. This reporter’s own kids didn’t get to bed until close to midnight — but they will tell you it was definitely worth staying up late for. Related Stories Business Disney+ Strikes Streaming Bundle and Content-Sharing Deal With Indonesia's Vidio Business Disney Entertainment TV Comms Chief Naomi Bulochnikov-Paul Departing The cheers were deafening inside the arena for the Worlds Collide tour, which features Malachi Barton ( Zombies 4, Camp Rock 3 ), Liamani Segura ( Descendants: Wicked Wonderland , Camp Rock 3 ), Dara Reneé ( Descendants: The Rise of Red ), Mekonnen Knife ( Zombies 4 ), Hudson Stone ( Camp Rock 3 ), Swayam Bhatia ( Zombies 4 ), Kiara Romero ( Descendants: Wicked Wonderland ) and Alexandro Byrd ( Descendants: Wicked Wonderland ). Among the set list were such songs as “It’s On,” “One Beat Away,” “Play My Music” and “We Rock” from the Camp Rock movies; “Like the Zombies Do,” “The Place to Be,” “Ain’t No Doubt About It” and “Someday” from the Zombies franchise; and “Perfect Princess,” “Chillin’ Like a Villain,” “Rotten to the Core” and “Ways to Be Wicked” from the Descendants soundtracks. Renée brought the house down with her powerful rendition of “Evil Like Me” from Descendants (sung by Kristin Chenoweth and Dove Cameron in the original), while Barton brought out his guitar for “Tomorrow” from Camp Rock 3, a song he said he’d begged to be allowed to perform. Stone, who also performed with his guitar, noted he’s the youngest on the tour, at 14 years old, but held his own with the rest of them. (The other performers range in age from 17-26.) Even with numerous costume changes, the show moved quickly. Between the different songs, at times various cast members would come out and address the audience directly, giving words of encouragement and inspiration. For example, Romero and Byrd talked about embracing your cultural heritage, while Romero, Segura and Bhatia spoke about the importance of friendship. Each of the actors got their time to address the crowd directly, and on big screens were shown images and videos of all the performers when they were younger. Many of them talked about their earlier ambitions to be professional singers, actors and/or dancers. A few of them, including Reneé, Barton, Segura and Stone, also got their chance in the spotlight to perform original solo songs, including “Never Waste a Heartbreak” (Reneé), “Stay for the Credits” (Barton), “Talk” (Stone) and “All the Things I’ve Learned So Far” (Segura). (In a nice touch, merchandise being sold in the lobby included not only shirts with all of the performers together but also tees featuring each person individually.) Among the younger fanbase, Barton and Segura have emerged as big stars, and the crowd went wild for their duet of Camp Rock ‘s iconic “This Is Me,” originally performed by Demi Lovato and Joe Jonas in the movie. In a surprise moment, Barton, who also stars alongside Bhatia in Disney’s upcoming series Coven Academy, brought out the stars of that show, which debuts Thursday. The show included elaborate choreography and big numbers and set pieces along with quieter moments, including a medley around a faux campfire. Barton and Segura again dueted on a Camp Rock song, “Wouldn’t Change a Thing,” during that portion, which also featured Romero singing “If Only” (from Descendants ), Reneé and Byrd singing “So This is Love” (from Cinderella and Descendants: The Rise of Red ) and the entire group singing the Camp Rock chant. The Worlds Collide cast Courtesy Disney Concerts So what did the younger attendees think about the show? Here are some reviews from two in the target demo: Brianna, age 14: “It was really engaging. They really wanted you to stand up and dance and be part of it, like when they taught us all a dance. The music was really good. I liked how they sang songs from even the [previous] movies that a lot of them weren’t in, like ‘If Only’ and ‘Someday,’ which was my favorite Obviously, those songs are really good. I also liked how they brought out their own stuff, like Hudson Stone sang ‘Talk’ and ‘Stay for the Credits,’ which are both really good singles that they made. “I liked how they showed videos of them when they were younger, so like I feel like it could have like inspired some kids to pursue what they want to do in their life. They also had a lot of messages about positivity. It was really nice because I feel like they were inspiring all the kids. I think it was a good length with an intermission.” Brooklyn, age 11: “What I liked about the Worlds Collide tour is that I loved all their outfits, how they spread positivity to children and just telling you to be yourself, and I loved how they showed younger pictures of [the performers], and I thought that was really fun. I loved how they mixed the songs. They are really good singers and I loved it overall. They were just telling kids to be their self, and I thought that was really positive, and I really liked how they did that. “I also thought the costumes were really good because they had a theme for everything, and they all had matching outfits, and I thought that was really cool. My favorite song, if I had to choose one, it would probably be ‘Wouldn’t Change a Thing’ from Camp Rock, because it’s a really good song. I also liked how they walked through the audience too. I really enjoyed it overall, and it was a really good show.” The Worlds Collide tour hit the Kia Forum in Inglewood on Wednesday and next travels to the Honda Center in Anaheim on Thursday before leaving Southern California for stops around the U.S. and Canada. It’ll go global starting in December with stops in Mexico, Great Britain, Germany, France and more. THR

full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Starz Goes Dark On Verizon FiOS Amid Carriage Dispute Ynon Kreiz Anointed Co-CEO Of New Paramount-WBD; David Ellison Says Mega-Studio Is “Transformational Moment For Our Industry” Ex-Mattel CEO Ynon Kreiz In Line For High-Level Paramount Exec Post View All October 1, 2026 6:57am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Hearst Media Production Group has renewed CBS weekend educational series The Visioneers with Zay Harding for two more seasons, through 2028. The show was first announced by Hearst in March 2025. Season 3 of the 30-minute eco-adventure original, which is produced by the Hearst production division in partnership with the VoLo Foundation, will premiere on Saturday. Hosted by Harding, an international explorer, the show features scientists, engineers and everyday people who are creating sustainable environmental solutions. Related Stories Executives Hearst Corp. CEO Steven Swartz Expects "Strong Year" For TV Division, Hints At M&A At A+E Global, Local Stations News 'Lucky Dog: Down Under' Expands Pet Franchise In New CBS Weekend Block The series airs weekend mornings as part of the CBS WKND educational/informational programming block. Timeslots vary by market. Watch on Deadline Guests this season include actor Edward Norton; former NFL player and ocean-conservation advocate Kelvin Beachum; NASCAR driver Austin Green; and Luci Baines Johnson, daughter of Lady Bird Johnson. Episodes are set from the Great Barrier Reef to America’s ports, racetracks and wildflower fields. “Alongside our partners at VoLo Foundation, we’re proud to bring audiences two more seasons of The Visioneers,” HMPG President Bryan Curb said in a statement. “The show has struck a real chord with viewers, sharing stories that prove environmental stewardship can take many forms – and that building a more sustainable future can be an engaging, hands-on adventure.” Thais Lopez V., president of VoLo Foundation, said the series “shows that the solutions to our biggest challenges are already in the hands of people with the courage to imagine a better world and the determination to make it real.” HMPG’s slate includes more than 30 original series and hundreds of hours of content annually on broadcast networks, station groups, connected-TV and streaming platforms. Its library spans 85 series and 6,000 episodes, with content across 100 countries.
